To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) We present a novel hardware-based security monitor that can be attached to the outside the system via the system and PTM buses, and can detect code-reuse attacks (CRA) that manipulate the control flows of victim applications.

(1) we can use ARM CoreSight to implement an external monitor that can detect code-reuse attacks, which are a type of control-hijacking attacks; (2) our monitor is able to detect code-reuse based attacks in a wide variety of applications with a low overhead; and (3) our monitor can also be implemented as an efficient software-only monitor that runs on the host system, with the help of a hardware accelerator.

(1) we can use the ARM CoreSight program trace macrocell (PTM), a real-time tracing hardware component, to monitor and analyze the execution traces of victim applications, (2) the PTM is able to provide sufficient information to identify control flow hijacking attacks, and (3) we can use this hardware component to build an efficient external security monitor for detecting control flow hijacking in an ARM-based SoC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) how to use CoreSight PTMs to integrate security monitoring IPs into a SoC; (2) how to design hardware/software mixed solutions for security applications; (3) how to design a security monitor for detecting CRAs; (4) how to use the security monitor to protect the host system from CRAs; and (5) how to evaluate the effectiveness and overhead of our security monitor.

the following: (a) developing a hardware-based CRA monitor that can be deployed in a resource-rich environment, (b) developing a hardware/software mixed CRA monitor that can work on a resource-constrained platform, and (c) evaluating the performance and effectiveness of the developed monitors.
the following questions: (i) How to detect CRAs in real time? (ii) How to implement the CRA detection in hardware?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed solution is an external security monitor, which can be used to detect CRAs in an ARM-based SoC.
we present two CRA detection schemes that can be deployed on ARM-based SoC platforms, and the schemes are based on the CoreSight PTMs.
our proposed solutions provide an effective means of detecting CRAs and are applicable to a variety of embedded systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our hardware/software mixed solution provides a low-cost alternative for detecting CRA attacks, and the performance of the hardware-based solution is significantly higher.
we have demonstrated that it is feasible to use CoreSight PTMs for integrating CRA monitoring IPs in ARM-based SoCs.
the proposed solutions are effective for CRA monitoring in an ARM-based system and can be implemented with reasonable hardware cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARM CoreSight infrastructure can be effectively utilized for security applications, and the PTM can serve as a communication channel between an external monitor and the host processor.
the ARM CoreSight architecture can be used as a platform for developing external security monitors that can detect control flow hijacking attacks.
the ARM CoreSight program trace can be used for a wide variety of purposes other than real-time debugging and software tracing.
